reponse:
**What broke:** On Thursday Nov 12, from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40), customer dashboards showed stale data. Release ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB. With the 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped. The change went to all pods at once. [1]

Detection was slow. There was no consumer-lag alert, and the first signal was a Sentry out-of-memory alert at 09:14. A rollback to v2.13.3 at 10:05 fixed the cause, and the lag was fully drained by 12:27. [1]

**Data loss:** None. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late. Lior's reconciliation matched per-workspace event counts to the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC. [1][5] All workspaces saw delayed dashboards. Four customers contacted support: Orbitly, Zest Grocers and two trial accounts. [1]

**What's changing:**
- ingest#419, merged Nov 13, restored the 1 MB default. It also added a guard that refuses a batch larger than 25% of the container memory limit. The bulk import path keeps 10 MB through explicit config. [1][9]
- KES-431: page the on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes. Owner Noa, due Nov 20. [1][6]
- KES-432: send ingest config changes to the canary pool first. Owner Daniel, due Nov 27. [1]
- KES-433: raise the worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes. Owner Lior, due Nov 27. [1]

Orbitly has also asked for a service credit for the incident. Sam is checking the terms with finance. [3]
